THE PURPOSE OF THIS FUNDING OPPORTUNITY IS TO SECURE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT OF FORMAL PRIVACY METHODS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO DIFFERENTIAL PRIVACY, FOR SAMPLE SURVEYS. 
SCOPE OF WORK: 
1. RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT OF FORMAL PRIVACY MECHANISMS FOR THE SAMPLE SURVEYS. THE GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A FEASIBLE APPROACH TO PRODUCING FORMALLY PRIVATE VERSIONS OF COMMON SURVEY DATA PRODUCTS, SUCH AS CROSS-TABULATIONS AND MICRODATA. SAMPLE SURVEYS HAVE FEATURES THAT COMPLICATE THE APPLICATION OF FORMAL PRIVACY TECHNIQUES, INCLUDING:   SURVEY WEIGHTS   CONTROLS TO POPULATION ESTIMATES WITHIN GEOGRAPHIC HIERARCHIES   HIGH DIMENSIONALITY   MULTIPLE PUBLIC RELEASES WITH VARYING DETAIL   LONGITUDINAL DESIGNS THAT TRACK RESPONDENTS OVER TIME. 
2. ADVANCES IN FORMAL PRIVACY THEORY FOR SAMPLE SURVEYS THE GOAL IS TO RESEARCH HOW THE GUARANTEES AND REQUIREMENTS OF FORMAL PRIVACY METHODS INTERACT WITH PROCEDURES USED IN SAMPLE SURVEYS AND TO SUGGEST MODIFICATIONS TO SURVEY PRODUCTION PROCESSES AND/OR PUBLIC OUTPUTS THAT ACCOUNT FOR THESE INTERACTIONS. RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT COMMON SURVEY PRACTICES, SUCH AS ADJUSTMENTS FOR NON-RESPONSE AND CONTROLS TO POPULATION ESTIMATES, CAN INTERACT SUBSTANTIALLY WITH THE SENSITIVITY REQUIREMENTS OF COMMON DIFFERENTIAL PRIVACY MECHANISMS. OTHER RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT CERTAIN SAMPLING ALGORITHMS
CAN AMPLIFY THE PRIVACY GUARANTEE OF COMMON DIFFERENTIAL PRIVACY MECHANISMS, BUT HAS NOTSHOWN THIS EFFECT FOR SAMPLING ALGORITHMS USED IN MANY SURVEYS. THIS PROGRAM PRIORITY SEEKS RESEARCH THAT WILL A) SHOW HOW COMMON SURVEY SAMPLING TECHNIQUES, SUCH AS STRATIFICATION AND CLUSTERING, INTERACT WITH FORMAL PRIVACY GUARANTEES B) ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY OF APPLYING ALTERNATIVE FORMAL PRIVACY DEFINITIONS, SUCH AS THOSE DERIVED UNDER THE PUFFERFISH FRAMEWORK, TO SAMPLE SURVEYS
C) SHOW HOW ADJUSTMENTS TO PARTICULAR PRODUCTION PROCESSES IN SURVEYS CAN IMPROVE
OUTCOMES FOR KNOWN FORMAL PRIVACY MECHANISMS. 
3. TRAINING AND OUTREACH FOR FORMAL PRIVACY THE GOAL IS TO EXPAND PUBLIC UNDERSTANDING OF FORMAL PRIVACY IN RELATION TO SAMPLE SURVEYS AND TO IMPROVE AND PROMOTE DISCUSSION OF THE MERITS OF FORMAL PRIVACY FOR PROTECTING RESPONDENT IDENTITIES AND ATTRIBUTES IN SAMPLE SURVEYS. DISCUSSIONS RELATED TO THE RELEASE OF TEST PRODUCTS FOR THE 2020 CENSUS HAVE SHOWN THAT DATA USERS HAVE DEEP CONCERNS ABOUT THE EFFECTS OF FORMAL PRIVACY ON SURVEY AND CENSUS OUTPUT, BUT HAVE ALSO SHOWN THAT DISCUSSIONS WOULD BENEFIT FROM A BETTER BASELINE UNDERSTANDING OF THE GOALS AND GUARANTEES OF FORMAL PRIVACY. THIS PROGRAM PRIORITY SEEKS RESEARCHERS THAT WILL A) HOLD SEMINARS AND WORKSHOPS WITH SURVEY DATA USERS TO ELICIT USE CASES FOR SURVEY DATA AND IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW THESE USE CASES INTERACT WITH FORMAL PRIVACY  B) DEVELOP RESOURCES, SUCH AS ONLINE PRIMERS AND COLLABORATIVE CODING ENVIRONMENTS, THAT SURVEY ADMINISTRATORS AND SURVEY DATA USERS CAN ACCESS TO FURTHER THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF FORMAL PRIVACY
C) MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS TO SURVEY ADMINISTRATORS ON PRODUCTION PRACTICES THAT HELP ENABLE THE USE OF FORMAL PRIVACY IN SURVEYS. D) MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS TO USERS OF FEDERAL AND NON-FEDERAL SURVEY DATA ON HOW TO ADAPT THEIR ANALYSES FOR FORMALLY PRIVATE PUBLIC SURVEY RELEASES E) MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS TO SURVEY DATA USERS WITH ACCESS TO NON-PUBLIC SURVEY DATA ON HOW TO ADJUST THEIR ANALYSES TO AVOID CONFLICT WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF FORMAL PRIVACY.
